filename: Probabilistic Data Assimilation for Ensemble Distribution Projections With Generative Machine Learning_ A Lorenz ’96 Proof-of-Concept.pdf
title: Probabilistic Data Assimilation for Ensemble Distribution Projections With Generative Machine Learning: A Lorenz ’96 Proof-of-Concept
testbed_rationale: The dataset is synthetic output from a low-dimensional toy chaotic model (Lorenz '96) used as an idealized proof-of-concept rather than Earth system benchmark simulation or observation data.
pain_points: High computational cost of unrolling long-term trajectories in numerical models to sample state distributions.
Chaotic drift and attractor differences when using standard short-term trajectory matching for climate timescales.
Assumption of stationarity/quasi-stationarity in the state distribution, which fails in non-stationary real-world climate systems.
Extending 1D distribution emulation to high-dimensional systems with non-linear multi-variable interactions.
Sensitivity to initial condition uncertainty and its propagation in complex dynamical systems.
extraction_notes: The paper presents a distribution-driven data assimilation framework using conditional normalizing flows to emulate equilibrium state distributions and infer physical parameters (forcing F) via Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) minimization.
